item.title: Eastleigh District Council records 36 suspensions in latest taxi and private hire enforcement report
item.description: Eastleigh District Council has recorded 125 enforcement outcomes across its taxi and private hire licensing function between 27 June 2025 and 31 January 2026, with suspensions accounting for the largest share of formal action. According to a report prepared for the Transport Forum , 36 suspensions were issued during the reporting period, making it the most frequently applied sanction. item.title: Bright lights, big problem: Night-time taxi drivers and motorist under strain
item.description: Taxi and private hire drivers working night shifts are facing mounting concerns over headlight glare, as new research from the RAC indicates that more than half of motorists believe the problem has intensified over the past year. According to the RAC’s latest survey, 57% of all drivers who experience headlight dazzle say it has worsened in the last 12 months, with only 31% disagreeing. item.title: BILKING IN TAXIS: Legal position, police response and what drivers can do
item.description: Bilking, the act of making off without paying a taxi or private hire fare, remains a recurring issue for drivers across the UK, with cases regularly reported and prosecuted under criminal law rather than treated as civil debt disputes. For drivers, that distinction is critical, influencing how incidents are reported and pursued. item.title: Smoking and vaping rules in licensed taxis and private hire vehicles explained for drivers and passengers
item.description: Smoking in licensed taxis and private hire vehicles has long been prohibited across the UK, but confusion remains among some drivers and passengers about whether vaping is treated the same way and what enforcement powers apply. Under the Health Act 2006 and subsequent smoke-free regulations in England, smoking is banned in any vehicle used for work purposes if more than one person uses the vehicle, regardless of whether they are present at the same time.
